### docs/agents/issue-tracker.md
# Issue tracker: GitHub

Issues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title "..." --body "..."`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.
- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body "..."`
- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label "..."` / `--remove-label "..."`
- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment "..."`

Infer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.

## Pull requests as a triage surface

**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_

When set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:

- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.
- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).
- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.

GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Run `gh issue view <number> --comments`.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.
- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.
- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.
- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.
- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body "<answer>"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.

### docs/agents/domain.md
# Domain Docs

How the engineering skills should consume this repo's domain documentation when exploring the codebase.

## Before exploring, read these

- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root, or
- **`CONTEXT-MAP.md`** at the repo root if it exists: it points at one `CONTEXT.md` per context. Read each one relevant to the topic.
- **`docs/adr/`**: read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.

If any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.

## File structure

Single-context repo (most repos):

```
/
├── CONTEXT.md
├── docs/adr/
│   ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
│   └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

Multi-context repo (presence of `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the root):

```
/
├── CONTEXT-MAP.md
├── docs/adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
└── src/
    ├── ordering/
    │   ├── CONTEXT.md
    │   └── docs/adr/                  ← context-specific decisions
    └── billing/
        ├── CONTEXT.md
        └── docs/adr/
```

## Use the glossary's vocabulary

When your output names a domain concept (in an issue title, a refactor proposal, a hypothesis, a test name), use the term as defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Don't drift to synonyms the glossary explicitly avoids.

If the concept you need isn't in the glossary yet, that's a signal: either you're inventing language the project doesn't use (reconsider) or there's a real gap (note it for `/domain-modeling`).

## Flag ADR conflicts

If your output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding:

> _Contradicts ADR-0007 (event-sourced orders), but worth reopening because…_

# Tech stack

- **[Entire](https://docs.entire.io/)** — Agent context capture, session history, and review tooling integrated with this repo's agent workflows.
- **[Vinext](https://vinext.dev/)** — Vite plugin that re-implements the Next.js 16 API surface (App Router, RSC, server actions) and targets Cloudflare Workers.

- **[Wrangler](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/)** — CLI for local Cloudflare Workers development and deployment.
- **[Cloudflare D1](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/)** — Serverless SQLite database used by the worker `DB` binding.
- **[Drizzle ORM / Drizzle Kit](https://orm.drizzle.team/)** — Type-safe SQL-like ORM and migration tooling (see `db/schema.ts` and `drizzle.config.ts`).
- **[Tailwind CSS v4](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/)** — Utility-first CSS framework.
- **[TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/)** — Typed JavaScript.
- **[ESLint](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/)** — Linting and code quality.
- **[Node.js test runner](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html)** — Built-in test runner used in `npm test`.

   102	
   103	**Adopted wholesale — these are better than what I had, don't water them down:**
   104	
   105	- **The claim/record separation.** "What the supplier said" is a *claim*, never a fact; "what our records say" is the trusted baseline. My earlier draft merged both into one `Quote` blob, which would have quietly destroyed the product's whole point. The models below keep them separate.
   106	- `stock_status` **with "in stock but already allocated to another customer."** This is the sharpest idea in the spec.    111	**What this plan adds — and why it's not optional:**
   112	
   113	The foundation spec explicitly puts comparison and decision-making out of scope: *"It never compares those claims against the factory's own records or makes any purchasing decision."* That's the right call for Plan 1, but **the Cognition track grades exactly that layer** — the autonomous decision and the artifact it produces. Foundation-only, we have a well-engineered call-logging tool and no answer to "where does Devin do the work?" So Plan 2 (§5, §6 Slice D) is the graded deliverable, not a nice-to-have. Plan 1 is the substrate; Plan 2 is the submission.

   116	
   117	1. **Demo scale.** The spec's demo data is 12 units needed / 4 on hand → shortfall of **8 units**. ### docs/checklist-api.md
     1	# The checklist API
     2	
     3	The cockpit no longer tries to show what the agent is *doing* — it shows what it
     4	has *finished*. That is a to-do list: eight fixed headers that exist from the
     5	moment a case is opened, plus one line per supplier that only appears once the
     6	agent decides that supplier is worth screening or calling.
     7	
     8	Fixed so the frontend can be designed before a run exists. Dynamic underneath so
     9	the number of suppliers is still the agent's call.
    10	
    11	## The read model
    12	
    13	`GET /cases/{case_id}/plan` → `CasePlan`
    14	
    15	```jsonc
    16	{
    17	  "case_id": "CASE-001",
    18	  "active_step_id": "outreach:SUP-RUL",
    19	  "done": 12,
    20	  "total": 20,
    21	  "sections": [
    22	    {
    23	      "group": "outreach",
    24	      "label": "Calling suppliers",          // fixed, never changes
    25	      "status": "active",                    // derived from the steps below
    26	      "steps": [
    27	        { "step_id": "outreach:brief", "label": "Writing the call brief", "status": "done" },
    28	        { "step_id": "outreach:SUP-KBY", "label": "Calling Kugellager Bayern GmbH",
    29	          "status": "done", "detail": "free_in_stock, 500,000 pcs at EUR 3.50",
    30	          "supplier_ref": "SUP-KBY", "dynamic": true }
    31	      ]
    32	    }
    33	  ]
    34	}
    35	```
    36	
    37	Section status is derived, never posted: `active` if any step is active, `done`
    38	when every step has finished (a `failed` or `skipped` step still counts as
    39	finished — a rejected supplier must not leave the header spinning forever),
    40	otherwise `pending`.
    41	
    42	Statuses are `pending`, `active`, `done`, `failed`, `skipped`.
    43	
    44	The eight headers, in order:
    45	
    46	| group | header |
    47	| --- | --- |
    48	| `intake` | Reading the incident |
    49	| `erp` | Pulling part data |
    50	| `suppliers` | Finding registered suppliers |
    51	| `screening` | Screening against procurement policy |
    52	| `outreach` | Calling suppliers |
    53	| `claims` | Collecting answers |
    54	| `costing` | Pricing every option |
    55	| `review` | Handing a ranked shortlist to the buyer |
    56	
    57	The eleven steps seeded with the case: `intake:incident`, `erp:part`,
    58	`erp:stock`, `erp:open_pos`, `erp:price_history`, `suppliers:list`,
    59	`screening:policy`, `outreach:brief`, `claims:normalise`, `costing:landed`,
    60	`review:package`.
    61	
    62	## The write model
    63	
    64	`POST /tools/plan/step?case_id=…&step_id=…&status=…` — one transition. Optional
    65	`detail`, and `group` + `label` + `supplier_ref` when the id is new.
    66	
    67	```
    68	POST /tools/plan/step?case_id=CASE-001&step_id=erp:part&status=active
    69	POST /tools/plan/step?case_id=CASE-001&step_id=erp:part&status=done&detail=6204-2RS%2C%200.11%20kg
    70	```
    71	
    72	`POST /tools/plan/steps?case_id=…` with a JSON list of the same fields — the
    73	fan-out door. Five suppliers being called at once is one request, and they all
    74	appear in the same poll instead of trickling in.
    75	
    76	```jsonc
    77	[
    78	  { "step_id": "outreach:SUP-KBY", "group": "outreach",
    79	    "label": "Calling Kugellager Bayern", "supplier_ref": "SUP-KBY", "status": "active" },
    80	  { "step_id": "outreach:SUP-RUL", "group": "outreach",
    81	    "label": "Calling Rulmenti", "supplier_ref": "SUP-RUL", "status": "active" }
    82	]
    83	```
    84	
    85	Both return the whole `CasePlan`, so a caller never has to read back.
    86	
    87	Rules the endpoints enforce:
    88	
    89	- **Idempotent on `step_id`.** A retry updates the line; it never adds a second
    90	  one. This is what makes it safe for an agent that repeats itself.
    91	- **A new id needs a `label` and a `group`**, or it is a 422. An unlabelled line
    92	  on a screen a human is watching is worse than a missing one.
    93	- **`started_at` / `completed_at` are set by the backend**, not the caller.
    94	- Every transition is also appended to the event log, so the existing event dock
    95	  and the checklist can never disagree.
    96

    98	
    99	Both paths write the same list, which is why the recorded demo and a live run
   100	look identical:
   101	
   102	- `backend/flow/conductor.py` — the deterministic run, sub-second, used on stage.
   103	- The Devin session — instructed in `backend/launch/devin.py::session_prompt`
   104	  with the exact ids above and the naming convention for dynamic ones
   105	  (`screening:<SUPPLIER_REF>`, `outreach:<SUPPLIER_REF>`).
   106	
   107	Held-back supplier: `POST /flow/run?hold_for=SUP-KBY` leaves that supplier's
   108	outreach line `active` with detail "holding for the live call" — which is
   109	precisely the frame the video pauses on before the phone rings.
   110	
   111	## Storage
   112	
   113	`cases/<case_id>/plan.json`, beside `events.jsonl`. Written atomically; a
   114	corrupt row is dropped on read rather than taking the screen down mid-demo.

   198	The single most important artifact of the weekend. Pydantic models, reviewed by everyone for 15 minutes, then **frozen**; later changes need a group ping. Types extend the foundation spec's vocabulary — `Incident`, `SupplierRecord` and `Claim` keep their spec meanings.

   202	Incident       = { case_id, part_id, qty_required, qty_on_hand, line_stop_at,

   205	                   part_id, approved, preferred, contract_unit_price: Decimal,
   206	                   standard_lead_days, certification, certification_expires_at,

   208	Claim          = { supplier_id, round, call_id, qty_offered, earliest_ready_text,

   222	PriceBreak  = { min_qty, unit_price: Decimal }

   241	
   242	This is the best answer to "why does this need an *engineer* and not a chatbot": the answer is **a model with tests**, and the recommendation is only trustworthy because the tests pass.
   243	
   244	`cost_model.py` — pure functions, `Decimal` throughout, fully unit-tested:
   245	
   246	```python
   247	goods_cost(qty, price_breaks)       # step function; a big order may cross a 25% break
   248	freight(weight_kg, mode, origin)    # air vs sea vs road; part weight × qty
   249	duty(hs_code, origin_country)       # tariff by origin
   250	carrying_cost(qty_ahead, unit, days_held, wacc)   # the cost of taking the discount
   251	expedite(claim, days_saved)         # surcharge to beat the line stop
   252	line_stop_cost(hours)               # what the shortage costs if we do nothing
   253	landed_cost(claim, qty, mode) -> LandedCost
   254	```
   255	
   256	Four decisions Devin then makes on top of the model — each a genuine trade-off:
   257	
   258	1. **Quantity-break vs. carrying cost.** A 25% break at high volume is only real if warehousing plus tied-up capital costs less than the discount. `carrying_cost` is what turns naive "buy more, it's cheaper" into an actual optimum.
   259	2. **Split sourcing to beat the deadline.** The demo's best beat: *air-freight 20% from the expensive supplier to cover the line-stop date, sea-freight the remaining 80% from the cheap one.* Total cost beats either single-source option. A pure LLM won't find this; a model plus a search over strategies will.
   260	3. **Cheapest unit price ≠ cheapest landed cost.** MOQ overshoot, freight on a heavy part and duty by origin routinely reorder the ranking.
   261	4. **Risk-weighted lead time, and claims you shouldn't trust.** A confidence-0.2 claim of 8 days from an unaudited new supplier is not the same as an incumbent's 10 — and `in_stock_allocated` means the units aren't ours at all. This is exactly where the claim/record separation pays off.

   361	## 8. MVP cut — what the UI actually is for the hackathon
   362	
   363	Added after review. §4 above is the *level-up* target; this section is what gets built this weekend. The reasoning is that the UI is **not the graded deliverable** — the Cognition track grades Devin's autonomy, the self-checking suites and the PR. The cockpit's only job is to make four minutes of invisible agent work legible, and to land the punchline. Every hour spent on it past that point is an hour not spent on Slice D.
   364	
   365	### 8.1 The decision: one page, progressively revealed, driven by a recorded event log
   366	
   367	**One route. No dashboard, no case list, no tabs, no dynamic segment.** `app/cockpit/page.tsx`, `CASE-001` hardcoded with a `?case=` override.
   368	
   369	```
   370	┌────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
   371	│  stockout · CASE-001 · 6204-2RS · ⏱ 11d04h │              │
   372	├────────────────────────────────────────────┤  event dock  │
   373	│  ① Shortage      [Launch sourcing agent]   │  14:02 ●     │
   374	│  ② Candidates    6 found · 3 rejected      │  14:02 ●     │
   375	│  ③ Calls         3 placed · stock status   │  14:03 ●     │
   376	│  ④ Claims        said vs. our records      │  14:05 ●     │
   377	│  ⑤ Cost          4 strategies compared     │  …           │
   378	│  ⑥ Decision      → the pull request        │              │
   379	└────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────┘
   380	          max 880px, sections mount in sequence      320px
   381	```
   382	
   383	**The mechanic that replaces four screens:** before launch only ① is visible. Press *Launch sourcing agent* and the recorded event log streams at 4×; each section mounts with a fade+slide as its stage arrives, and the page auto-scrolls to the newest one. Pressing one button and watching the story write itself down the screen *is* the "agent is working" feeling — it does the job of the dashboard, the timeline page and the live-calls page at once, and it costs a fraction of them.
   384	
   385	Why this is the right MVP shape:
   386	
   387	- **Zero routing work.** No route transitions, no per-route loading or error states, no `[caseId]` plumbing, no nav that can be clicked into a dead end mid-demo.
   388	- **The narrative order is the DOM order.** The page can't get out of sync with the pitch, because it *is* the pitch.
   389	- **It degrades silently.** A section with no data simply never appears. A half-finished cost engine on Saturday night costs us a section, not a broken page.
   390	- **Fully offline and deterministic.** No backend, no network, no ACUs, no venue wifi.
   391

   393	
   394	`make record` captures a real end-to-end run's `events.jsonl` and case artifacts into `demo/fixtures/`; the committed fixture is that recording. `?replay=4` plays it back through the same code path live polling would use.

   396	This matters for how it's framed: *"this is Tuesday's run played back at 4× — here's the commit that recorded it, and here's the live PR it opened. We can run it cold in 90 seconds afterwards if you'd like."* That is a stronger answer than a live run that might stall on stage, and it is honest — nothing on screen is invented.

     1	# Slice B — core API, system of record, seed data (+ the cockpit route)
     2	
     3	Everything in this slice is **additive**. No file that existed before it was
     4	moved, renamed or edited; `app/globals.css`, `app/layout.tsx`, `app/page.tsx`
     5	and `components/theme-provider.tsx` are exactly as the team left them.
     6	
     7	## Run it
     8	
     9	```bash
    10	./run.sh setup   # once per machine: venv deps, npm install, build the database
    11	./run.sh         # API + cockpit together. Ctrl-C stops both.
    12	./run.sh ui      # cockpit only — runs offline, this is the demo path
    13	./run.sh test    # 87 backend tests + typecheck. Never touches the network.
    14	```
    15	
    16	Cockpit at `/cockpit`; API docs at `/docs` on whichever port it picked.
    17	
    18	## What this slice adds
    19	
    20	| Path | |
    21	|---|---|
    22	| `packages/contracts/` | the frozen contract — Pydantic models, and the JSON Schema + TypeScript generated from them |
    23	| `backend/record/` | system of record: two adapters behind one interface, plus the seed data |
    24	| `backend/store/` | case store and append-only event log |
    25	| `backend/api/` | one FastAPI process: Devin tool endpoints + cockpit read API |
    26	| `backend/detect/` | shortage detector |
    27	| `backend/tests/` | 87 tests |
    28	| `app/cockpit/` | the cockpit route + its own scoped stylesheet |
    29	| `components/cockpit/` | cockpit components |
    30	| `lib/api/`, `lib/contracts.ts`, `lib/fixtures/`, `lib/format.ts`, `lib/stages.ts` | data layer and generated types |
    31	| `cases/` | runtime output — the artifact *is* the datastore |
    32	
    33	**Design tokens are scoped to the route.** `app/cockpit/cockpit.css` carries the
    34	DESIGN.md palette and is loaded only on `/cockpit`, so nothing in Slice B
    35	requires editing `app/globals.css`, which the landing page shares.
    36	
    37	Build artifacts are kept out of git by `backend/.gitignore` and
    38	`packages/.gitignore` — the root `.gitignore` is untouched.
    39	
    40	## The system of record
    41	
    42	`SystemOfRecord` (`backend/record/ports.py`) is the plug-in point. Two adapters
    43	implement it and **both run against the same test suite**, which is what makes
    44	"swapping in a real ERPNext is one adapter class" demonstrable rather than a
    45	claim:
    46	
    47	| Adapter | Backing | |
    48	|---|---|---|
    49	| `SqliteERP` | `backend/record/supplyguard.db`, ERPNext-shaped tables | default |
    50	| `MockERP` | `backend/record/demo_data/*.yaml` | reference implementation, and the seed source |
    51	
    52	The YAML is what a human edits; `./run.sh db` compiles it into SQLite. The `.db`
    53	is a build artifact and is gitignored. Switch with `RECORD_BACKEND=yaml|sqlite`.
    54	
    55	Money is stored as `TEXT`, never `REAL` — SQLite's `REAL` is a float, and a float
    56	cent error is invisible in a demo and fatal in procurement.
    57	
    58	**Opening the database in a Windows GUI:** `./run.sh db-export`. DB Browser
    59	cannot open it in place — the repo is on ext4 inside WSL and Windows reaches
    60	that over `\\wsl.localhost`, which has no POSIX file locking, so SQLite reports
    61	*"database is locked"* whatever is running. `db-export` writes a `VACUUM INTO`
    62	snapshot to your Windows Downloads folder.
    63	
    64	Case artifacts deliberately stay files. `cases/<id>/` is Git, not SQL, because
    65	the procurement-as-code thesis is that the artifact *is* the datastore.
    66	
    67	## Ground rules this slice enforces
    68	
    69	- **Phone numbers** validated to E.164 on entry, masked everywhere else. No API
    70	  model has a field for a raw number. `backend/tests/test_no_raw_phones.py`
    71	  scans every endpoint.
    72	- **Rehearsal is the default.** Live calling needs `LIVE_CALLS` set to exactly
    73	  `yes-place-real-calls`. Never a fallback.
    74	- **"Unknown" is a first-class answer**, and filing a claim never raises.
    75	- **Money is `Decimal`**, serialized as a string. No float arithmetic.
    76	- **No real phone numbers.** Seed numbers use the German BNetzA drama range.

docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:5:## What SupplyGuard Is, In One Paragraph
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:7:A factory is short on a part it needs. SupplyGuard phones the factory's approved suppliers, asks each one specific questions about that part, and writes down what they say as a structured record — never as a decision. Separately, SupplyGuard already knows what the factory's own paperwork says about each supplier (contract price, agreed lead time, certification status, and how much stock is already promised to other customers). The foundation layer built in this plan does not yet compare the two. It just makes sure both sides — "what the supplier said" and "what our records say" — exist as clean, trustworthy, separately-typed information. Comparing them and making a decision is a later phase.
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:13:- **What our own records say about a supplier.** This comes from the factory's own systems (its ERP, its supplier database). It's the trusted baseline — contract price, lead time, certification expiry, how many units are already spoken for.
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:24:3. **The system of record** — what the factory's own files say about each supplier: their contract price, their agreed delivery time, their certification, and how many units they've already promised elsewhere. This is the trusted baseline that a supplier's phone claim will eventually be checked against. It's built so that a company can plug in their own real system (their ERP) later, by implementing just two simple lookups, without changing anything else.
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:97:## Building Block 3: The System Of Record (and the plug-in point for a real ERP)
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:99:**Purpose:** Hold the factory's own trusted facts about its suppliers, and be the "second source" that a phone claim eventually gets checked against. Also define, in the smallest possible terms, how a real company would connect their actual inventory/ERP system in place of the demo data.
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:114:**The plug-in point, explained simply:** the "system of record" is described as a contract with exactly two capabilities — "look up approved suppliers for a part" and "look up an incident by id." Anything that can answer those two questions correctly counts as a valid system of record, whether it's backed by a small local database (as the demo is) or by a company's real inventory system, or even by something as simple as a JSON export with no database behind it at all. This is intentionally *not* a plugin marketplace with configuration files and auto-discovery — it's a minimal, two-question contract that a company implements once, against whatever system they already run, and the rest of SupplyGuard doesn't need to know or care which one is behind it.
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:116:**The demo data** seeds four fictional suppliers across four countries, three of them approved for the same part number (used to prove that ordering and filtering both work correctly) and one on a different part number entirely (used to prove that a supplier for the wrong part is correctly excluded). The demo shortage describes needing twelve units of a part while only four are on hand — a shortfall of eight, which becomes the number every later phase of SupplyGuard is trying to close.
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:124:**Purpose:** Define exactly what gets said out loud on a call, and exactly what shape the answer must come back in, so a phone conversation turns into clean structured data rather than a paragraph of prose that has to be interpreted later.
docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md:171:- It does not involve any language model or AI reasoning yet — this layer is purely about safely capturing and structuring data, not interpreting or judging it.

Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo owner/name
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (positional or --checkpoint) and a
                 checkpoint that has been pushed.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;

   150	        "//",
   151	        "// These types come from the Pydantic models in packages/contracts/models.py,",
   152	        "// which are also what CALL-E receives as `recipient_result_schema`. One source of",
   153	        "// truth, three consumers.",
   154	        "//",

   157	        "",
   158	    ]
   159	
   160	    for name, enum_cls in sorted(ENUMS.items()):
   161	        members = " | ".join(f'"{m.value}"' for m in enum_cls)
   162	        out.append(f"export type {name} = {members}")
   163	    out.append("")
   164	
   165	    for name, model in sorted(MODELS.items()):

   414	def cmd_db_export(dest: str | None) -> None:
   415	    """Copy the database somewhere a desktop GUI can open it.
   416	
   417	    A GUI cannot always open the file in place. Under WSL the repo is on ext4 and
   418	    Windows reaches it over \\\\wsl.localhost, which has no POSIX file locking, so
   419	    SQLite reports "database is locked" whatever is running. VACUUM INTO takes a
   420	    consistent snapshot rather than a byte copy that could catch a half-write.
   421	    """
   422	    py = ensure_python()
   423	    ensure_db(py)
   424	
   425	    if dest:
   426	        target = Path(dest)
   427	    else:
   428	        # Under WSL, land it on the Windows side where the GUI lives.
   429	        windows_homes = sorted(Path("/mnt/c/Users").glob("*/Downloads")) if Path("/mnt/c/Users").is_dir() else []
   430	        skip = {"All Users", "Default", "Default User", "Public"}
   431	        windows_homes = [p for p in windows_homes if p.parent.name not in skip]
   432	        target = windows_homes[0] / "supplyguard.db" if windows_homes else Path.home() / "supplyguard.db"
   433	
   434	    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   435	    if target.exists():
   436	        target.unlink()
   437	    code = (
   438	        "import sqlite3, sys;"
   439	        "c = sqlite3.connect('backend/record/supplyguard.db');"
   440	        "c.execute('VACUUM INTO ?', (sys.argv[1],));"
   441	        "c.close()"
   442	    )
   443	    subprocess.run([str(py), "-c", code, str(target)], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
   444	    ok(f"snapshot written ({target.stat().st_size // 1024} KB)")
   445	    dim(f"  {target}")
   446	    if shutil.which("wslpath"):
   447	        win = subprocess.run(["wslpath", "-w", str(target)], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
   448	        if win:
   449	            dim(f"  Windows  {win}")
   450	    print("\n  Open that path in your SQLite browser. It is a copy: edits there do not")
   451	    print("  reach the repo, and `python run.py db` rebuilds the real one from the YAML.\n")
   452

   462	    "fixtures": lambda a: cmd_fixtures(),

---
name: conductor
description: Configure, operate, and troubleshoot Conductor — workspaces, repository settings.toml files, scripts, files to copy, managed settings, agent controls, and review workflows. Use when helping someone set up or operate Conductor.
license: Proprietary
compatibility: Conductor runs coding agents in isolated workspaces, either locally in git worktrees on the user's Mac or in Linux cloud sandboxes.
---

# Conductor

Conductor is an app for running multiple coding agents in parallel, each in an isolated workspace. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor Agent, and OpenCode. The desktop app is Mac-only; cloud workspaces run on Linux and can be driven from the Mac app, the iOS app, or the public API.

This file covers the facts that are easy to get wrong. For anything else, fetch the docs page linked in the relevant section.

## Know your environment

Check `CONDUCTOR_IS_LOCAL` before giving environment-specific guidance: `1` = you are running locally on the user's Mac; `0` = you are in a Conductor cloud sandbox (Linux).

- **Local**: your session runs in a git worktree on the user's Mac, with the user's local permissions. Each repository has a main root directory and one worktree per workspace. New workspaces are created from the repository's configured base branch; Conductor fetches from `origin` first, so a workspace starts from the latest remote commit even when the local checkout is behind (the fetch does not move the branch checked out in the root directory).
- **Cloud**: your session runs in a Linux sandbox with a single checkout of the repository. You have no access to the user's machine or its filesystem — unless the Conductor `RunLocalCommand` tool is available, which runs a one-shot shell command on the user's Mac. Cloud workspaces can be created from the Mac app, the iOS app, or the API, so do not assume a Mac client.

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/concepts/workspaces-and-branches
- https://conductor.build/docs/concepts/workflow
- https://conductor.build/docs/concepts/parallel-agents

## Settings files

1. Machine-local, one repository: `<repo>/.conductor/settings.local.toml`.
2. Shared with the team: `<repo>/.conductor/settings.toml` — the Mac app reads it from the default branch on the remote, so merge it before it takes effect locally; cloud setup reads it from the branch the workspace is created from.
3. This user, all repositories: `~/.conductor/settings.toml`.
4. Organization-controlled: `~/.conductor/settings.managed.toml`.

Precedence: managed > repository local > repository shared > user > built-in defaults. Any TOML file outranks any legacy JSON file, regardless of layer; Conductor writes new settings as TOML.

Schemas:

- User settings: `https://conductor.build/schemas/settings.schema.json`
- Repository settings: `https://conductor.build/schemas/settings.repo.schema.json`
- Managed settings: `https://conductor.build/schemas/settings.toml.json`

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/settings
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/scripts/share-with-teammates

## Repository settings and scripts

A typical `<repo>/.conductor/settings.toml`:

```toml
"$schema" = "https://conductor.build/schemas/settings.repo.schema.json"

[scripts]
setup = "pnpm install"
run_mode = "concurrent"

[scripts.run.dev]
available_in = [ "local" ]
command = "pnpm dev --port $CONDUCTOR_PORT"
default = true
icon = "play"

[scripts.run.test]
command = "pnpm test:watch"
icon = "test-tube"
```

The schema and settings docs list every key. Facts worth knowing:

- Setup, run, and archive scripts run from the workspace directory in non-interactive shells: `zsh` on the user's Mac (with the login shell environment captured), `bash` in cloud workspaces. Put required toolchain setup in the scripts themselves rather than relying on interactive shell startup.
- Local workspaces get ten ports, `CONDUCTOR_PORT` through `CONDUCTOR_PORT+9`. `CONDUCTOR_PORT` is unset in cloud workspaces, so mark run scripts that depend on it `available_in = [ "local" ]`.
- Use `run_mode = "concurrent"` only when multiple workspaces can run at the same time (separate ports, no shared database or Docker stack); otherwise `nonconcurrent`.
- `scripts.run.<id>.available_in` takes `local`, `cloud`, or both; omit it to show the script everywhere.
- `icon` values are lowercase-kebab Lucide names; invalid names fall back to `play`.
- Legacy single-string `scripts.run` is still read and is migrated to `[scripts.run.<id>]` when Conductor rewrites the file.
- When one run script starts multiple processes, keep them in the same process group (e.g. `concurrently`) instead of backgrounding with `&`.
- Use Spotlight testing when a project cannot run from a worktree and must execute from the repository root.
- Settings that are not repository-configurable include model defaults, reasoning defaults, tool approvals, and the default workspace location — those live in user settings.

Environment variables available to scripts and agents:

- `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME`: Workspace name.
- `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_ID`: Workspace ID in agent and terminal processes. The `conductor` CLI uses it when a workspace argument is omitted.
- `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_PATH`: Workspace path.
- `CONDUCTOR_ROOT_PATH`: Repository root directory. In cloud workspaces this equals the workspace path.
- `CONDUCTOR_DEFAULT_BRANCH`: Default branch name. Local workspaces only.
- `CONDUCTOR_PORT`: First of the ten allocated ports. Local workspaces only.
- `CONDUCTOR_IS_LOCAL`: `1` on the user's Mac, `0` in a cloud workspace. Branch on this in `scripts.setup` for local-only steps.

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/scripts
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/scripts/setup
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/scripts/run
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/scripts/spotlight-testing
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/shells
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/environment-variables

## Files to copy

For static gitignored files (`.env` files, local config, certificates) that every new workspace needs, use Files to copy rather than a setup script. Resolution order:

1. `.worktreeinclude` at the repository root.
2. `file_include_globs` in repository settings.
3. Default `.env*` pattern.

Use `scripts.setup` when the workspace needs commands run: dependency installs, generated files, symlinks.

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/files-to-copy
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/worktreeinclude

## Managed settings

Organization-controlled settings live at `~/.conductor/settings.managed.toml` (legacy `settings.managed.json` is still read). Managed values override user and repository settings and disable the matching controls in Settings. Managed settings are provisional.

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/settings/managed
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/privacy
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/security-and-permissions

## Legacy conductor.json

The Mac client ignores repo-level `conductor.json` once `<repo>/.conductor/settings.toml` exists, but cloud setup still falls back to a `conductor.json` setup script when no settings TOML defines one — delete `conductor.json` once migrated. Migration map:

- `scripts.setup` -> `scripts.setup`
- `scripts.run` -> `scripts.run.<id>.command`
- `scripts.archive` -> `scripts.archive`
- `runScriptMode` -> `scripts.run_mode`
- `enterpriseDataPrivacy` -> `enterprise_data_privacy`

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/conductor-json

## Agent controls

Plan mode, fast mode, reasoning controls, Codex personality, checkpoints, MCP, slash commands, todos, and instruction files are covered in the docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/agent-behavior
- https://conductor.build/docs/concepts/agent-modes
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/checkpoints
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/mcp
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/slash-commands
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/todos

## Review and merge

When leaving review feedback from inside Conductor, use the Conductor `DiffComment` tool when it is available — comments appear in the app's Checks panel. Do not post review feedback to GitHub unless the user explicitly asks for GitHub comments.

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/guides/review-and-merge
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/diff-viewer
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/checks

## Troubleshooting

Non-obvious causes to check first:

- Setup or run scripts that depend on interactive shell startup behavior (they run in non-interactive shells).
- Missing files that are gitignored and should be copied via Files to copy or `.worktreeinclude`.
- A shared resource (fixed port, single database, Docker stack) that needs `run_mode = "nonconcurrent"` or Spotlight testing.
- Managed settings in `~/.conductor/settings.managed.toml` overriding what the user set.
- A legacy `conductor.json` being ignored by the Mac client because `.conductor/settings.toml` exists.

Docs:

- https://conductor.build/docs/faq
- https://conductor.build/docs/troubleshooting/issues
- https://conductor.build/docs/reference/shells

     5	A shortage is filed with an agent. It reads the system of record, screens

    12	[`docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md`](docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md)
    13	
    14	## Repo layout
    15	
    16	```
    17	packages/contracts/   The frozen contract. Pydantic models + the JSON Schema and
    18	                      TypeScript types generated from them. Shared by every
    19	                      slice; changes need a group ping.
    20	backend/              Slice B — the service.
    21	  record/             system of record — two adapters behind one interface:
    22	                      ERP seed data (YAML) + SQLite, schema.sql, seed data
    23	  store/              case store and append-only event log (cases/ is the database)
    24	  api/                one FastAPI process: Devin tool endpoints + cockpit read API
    25	  detect/             shortage detector (the no-human-in-the-loop trigger)
    26	  tests/              Slice B's tests
    27	ui/                   Slice A — the cockpit (Next.js). Runs with no backend.
    28	  app/api/cases/      Slice 1 launch API as Route Handlers, so a case can be
    29	                      started from a Vercel deployment with no Python process
    30	orchestrator/         the CLI that launches a case
    31	cases/                Runtime output. One directory per case; the artifact IS the datastore.
    32	test/                 Slice C's CALL-E smoke test
    33	docs/                 plans and specs
    34	```
    35	
    36	## Commands
    37	
    38	Works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux:
    39	
    40	```bash
    41	python run.py setup   # once per machine: venv, npm install, build the database
    42	python run.py         # the whole stack — API + cockpit. Ctrl-C stops both.
    43	python run.py ui      # cockpit only. Runs offline; this is the demo path.
    44	python run.py test    # backend tests + UI typecheck. Never touches the network.
    45	```
    46	
    47	| | |
    48	|---|---|
    49	| macOS / Linux | `python3 run.py …` — or `./run.sh …`, a thin wrapper |
    50	| Windows | `python run.py …` — or `run …`, which uses the `py` launcher |
    51	
    52	`run.py` bootstraps from a clean clone: it creates the virtualenv, installs
    53	dependencies, builds the database if missing, and picks free ports (API from
    54	8010, cockpit from 3000). Node >= 20.9 is the one thing it cannot install for
    55	you; if you use nvm it will tell you which version you already have.
    56	
    57	It is Python rather than a shell script because Python 3.11+ is already required
    58	by the backend, so every machine has it — whereas Windows has no `bash` and
    59	macOS ships bash 3.2.
    60	
    61	Other commands: `db`, `db-export`, `fixtures`, `build`. The `Makefile` mirrors
    62	them on Unix.
    63	
    64	The cockpit defaults to `REDACTED` and runs entirely
    65	offline. `./run.sh` points it at the live API instead.
    66	
    67	**Opening the database in a GUI on Windows:** run `python run.py db-export`. DB
    68	Browser for SQLite cannot open the file in place — the repo is on ext4 inside
    69	WSL, and Windows reaches that over `\\wsl.localhost`, which has no POSIX file
    70	locking, so SQLite reports *"database is locked"* regardless of what is running.
    71	`db-export` writes a `VACUUM INTO` snapshot to your Windows Downloads folder and
    72	prints the `C:\...` path to paste in.
    73	
    74	## Running SupplyOS end to end on main
    75	
    76	Verified from a clean clone on 2026-08-23 with Ubuntu 22.04, Node 20.18.1 and
    77	pyenv Python 3.12.8. The minimum versions are Python 3.11 and Node 20.9. If the
    78	system `python3` is older, invoke `run.py` with a 3.11+ interpreter explicitly.
    79	
    80	### 1. Set up once
    81	
    82	```bash
    83	git clone https://github.com/D4V1ND/ehl_hack.git
    84	cd ehl_hack
    85	python3.12 run.py setup
    86	```

    89	installs the UI packages, and seeds the ERP. On main, `calle-ai` is in
    90	`pyproject.toml`, so no separate `pip install -r requirements.txt` is needed.
    91	
    92	### 2. Check the offline path
    93	
    94	```bash
    95	python3.12 run.py test
    96	```
    97	
    98	This ran 292 backend tests and the UI typecheck during the clean-clone
    99	verification. It does not touch the network.
   100	
   101	### 3. Bring up the stack
   102	
   103	Start the API from the repository root:
   104	
   105	```bash
   106	.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn backend.api.main:app --port 8010

   116	```
   117	
   118	Check the safety mode before continuing:
   119	
   120	```bash
   121	curl -s localhost:8010/healthz
   122	```
   123	
   124	The response should contain `"call_mode":"rehearsal"`. Rehearsal is the safe
   125	default and does not dial anyone.
   126	
   127	### 4. Walk the case
   128	
   129	Open <http://localhost:3000/inventory> and choose **Source this part**, or drive
   130	the same flow directly through the API:
   131	
   132	```bash
   133	curl -s localhost:8010/inventory | head
   134	curl -s -X POST localhost:8010/cases \
   135	  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
   136	  -d '{"part_id":"PRT-6204"}'
   137	# On a clean clone this returns CASE-6204-2RS and a stub Devin session.
   138	
   139	curl -s -X POST \
   140	  "localhost:8010/flow/run?case_id=CASE-6204-2RS&hold_for=SUP-KBY"
   141	curl -s -X POST \
   142	  "localhost:8010/flow/call?case_id=CASE-6204-2RS&supplier_ref=SUP-KBY"
   143	curl -s -X POST \

   147	.venv/bin/python -m orchestrator.sourcing publish --case CASE-6204-2RS

   150	If that case ID already exists, `POST /cases` adds a numeric suffix; use the
   151	returned ID in the remaining commands. No `DEVIN_API_KEY` is needed for the
   152	stub session.
   153	
   154	In the verified rehearsal, the flow screened six suppliers and rejected three
   155	on policy (blocked origin, missing certification, and missing audit). It asked
   156	two suppliers, held `SUP-KBY` for the deliberate call, and recommended `STR-05`:
   157	a 4,000 + 6,500 split with EUR 17,078.27 landed cost that meets the line stop.
   158	Publishing produced a dry-run pull request containing six procurement
   159	artifacts.
   160	
   161	There is no `POST /flow/publish` route. Publishing uses either the CLI command
   162	above or `POST /tools/publish_pr?case_id=CASE-6204-2RS`.
   163	
   164	### 5. Enable live integrations only when needed
   165	
   166	For a real call, start the API with all four settings below and add `--live` to
   167	the CLI `call` command:
   168	
   169	```bash
   170	export CALLE_API_KEY=...
   171	export DEMO_CALL_DESTINATION='<your phone in E.164 format>'
   172	export LIVE_CALLS=yes-place-real-calls
   173	export FAKE_CALLS=0
   174	
   175	.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn backend.api.main:app --port 8010
   176	```
   177	
   178	Then place the call from another terminal:
   179	
   180	```bash
   181	.venv/bin/python -m orchestrator.sourcing call \
   182	  --case CASE-6204-2RS --supplier SUP-KBY --live
   183	```
   184	
   185	`DEMO_CALL_DESTINATION` must be the E.164 number that should receive every demo
   186	call. A call result can take roughly 18 minutes to arrive, so do not make the
   187	post-call repricing the demo finale.
   188	
   189	- Set `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_REPO` to make `publish` open a real pull request.
   190	- Set `DEVIN_API_KEY` to create a real Devin session from `POST /cases`.
   191	- Set `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` to the public `cloudflared` URL so that Devin can call
   192	  the local API back.
   193	
   194	## Opening a case for any part
   195	
   196	`GET /inventory` is every part in the item master with what is in the bin, how
   197	many days that covers, and whether a case is already open. `POST /cases
   198	{"part_id": "PRT-6204"}` opens one for a part: the shortage is derived from the
   199	records — bin, take rate, the BOM line that consumes it, the incumbent, a
   200	purchase order that has slipped — and a Devin session is started to work it. No
   201	`DEVIN_API_KEY` means a stub session and an open case, never a failed trigger.
   202	
   203	```bash
   204	python run.py api                                                        # :8010
   205	curl -s localhost:8010/inventory | head
   206	curl -s -X POST localhost:8010/cases -H 'content-type: application/json' \
   207	     -d '{"part_id": "PRT-6204"}'
   208	```
   209	
   210	In the UI that is `/inventory`: one button per row, which opens the case and
   211	follows it to `/cases/<id>`. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=live` and
   212	`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE` first — fixtures mode has nothing to trigger. The session
   213	is told to read the part, its stock, its open orders and its price history from
   214	the ERP *before* it looks at suppliers, and it is told not to order anything.
   215	
   216	`PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is what the session is given to call back on; at demo time
   217	that is the `cloudflared` URL, because the request origin is localhost.
   218	
   219	## Running a whole case
   220	
   221	One command does the unattended part: read the shortage, read the part, screen
   222	the approved suppliers, ask the ones that pass, price every plan and write the
   223	review package. `--hold-for` leaves one supplier uncalled so that call can be
   224	placed deliberately — that is the demo's live moment.
   225	
   226	```bash
   227	python run.py api                                                        # :8010
   228	python -m orchestrator.sourcing run     --case CASE-001 --hold-for SUP-KBY
   229	python -m orchestrator.sourcing call    --case CASE-001 --supplier SUP-KBY   # add --live to dial
   230	python -m orchestrator.sourcing collect --case CASE-001                      # files the answer, re-prices
   231	python -m orchestrator.sourcing state   --case CASE-001
   232	python -m orchestrator.sourcing publish --case CASE-001
   233	```
   234	
   235	The same steps are `POST /flow/run`, `POST /flow/call`, `POST /flow/collect`,
   236	`GET /flow/state`. Every stage appends an event, so the cockpit shows where the
   237	run has got to rather than a spinner.
   238	
   239	Calling is rehearsed unless live calling is switched on server-side
   240	(`LIVE_CALLS=yes-place-real-calls` **and** `FAKE_CALLS=0`); `--live` without that
   241	is refused with a `409` rather than silently rehearsing. `DEMO_CALL_DESTINATION`
   242	points *every* supplier call at one number, so a live run on stage reaches the
   243	phone in the room and cannot dial a real supplier by accident. Rehearsed answers are
   244	derived from the supplier's own record — contract price, standard lead time,
   245	historical fill minus known allocations — and are deterministic per case and
   246	supplier, so the demo tells the same story twice.
   247	
   248	`/flow/run` returns *every* costed plan, not just the winner: a buyer picks one.
   249	Nothing is ordered by the agent, and `publish` opens a pull request for a human
   250	to merge (rehearsed unless `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_REPO` are set).
   251	
   252	## Slice 1 — launch a case from the CLI
   253	
   254	The launch path that needs nothing but the Next app:
   255	
   256	```bash
   257	cd ui && npm install && npm run dev
   258	python -m orchestrator.run --case CASE-001 --api http://localhost:3000
   259	```
   260	
   261	- `POST /api/cases` — `{ "case_id": "CASE-001" }`, or an inline `incident`. Loads
   262	  the fixture, appends `created`, starts a Devin session, appends
   263	  `session_started`, returns `201`.
   264	- `GET /api/cases/CASE-001/events` — the append-only log.
   265	- `/cases/CASE-001` — polls it every 2s.
   266	
   267	Events live in a module-level map (`ui/lib/cases/store.ts`) because serverless has
   268	no durable disk; the durable case store is `backend/casestore/`. Money is only
   269	ever a decimal string. Without `DEVIN_API_KEY` the session is stubbed, so this
   270	never fails on a missing key and never places a phone call. Cross-origin browser
   271	access is opt-in via `CASES_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`.
   272	
   273	```bash
   274	cd ui && npm test   # route handlers, in-memory, no live Devin
   275	```
   276	
   277	## The system of record
   278	
   279	`SystemOfRecord` (`backend/record/ports.py`) is the plug-in point the spec
   280	describes. Two adapters implement it and **both are covered by the same test
   281	suite**, which is what makes "swapping in a real ERPNext is one adapter class"
   282	demonstrable rather than a claim:
   283	
   284	| Adapter | Backing | Use |
   285	|---|---|---|
   286	| `SqliteERP` | `backend/record/supplyguard.db`, ERPNext-shaped tables | default |
   287	| ERP | `backend/record/demo_data/*.yaml` | reference implementation, and the seed source |
   288	
   289	The YAML is what a human edits; `python run.py db` compiles it into SQLite. The
   290	database is a build artifact and is gitignored. Switch with `RECORD_BACKEND=yaml`
   291	or `RECORD_BACKEND=sqlite`.
   292	
   293	Money is stored as `TEXT`, never `REAL` — SQLite's `REAL` is a float, and a float
   294	cent error is invisible in a demo and fatal in procurement.
   295	
   296	Case artifacts deliberately do **not** live in SQL. `cases/<id>/` stays files in
   297	Git, because the procurement-as-code thesis is that the artifact *is* the
   298	datastore and a reviewer can walk it in a pull request.
   299	
   300	## Ground rules
   301	
   302	These hold for any code added to this repo:
   303	
   304	- **Phone numbers** are validated to E.164 on entry and masked everywhere else.
   305	  No API model has a field for a raw number; the one accessor that returns one is
   306	  `raw_phone_for_outreach`, for building an outbound call and nothing else.
   307	  `backend/tests/test_no_raw_phones.py` scans every endpoint for leaks.
   308	- **Rehearsal is the default.** Live calling requires `LIVE_CALLS` set to exactly
   309	  `yes-place-real-calls`. Never a fallback, never an unset variable.
   310	- **"Unknown" is a first-class answer**, and building a claim never raises — a
   311	  garbled call becomes a confidence-0 claim, not an exception.
   312	- **Money is `Decimal`**, serialized as a string. No float arithmetic anywhere.
   313	- **No real secrets or real phone numbers.** Seed numbers come from the German
   314	  BNetzA drama range and are never dialed.

     1	# CLAUDE.md
     2	
     3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4	
     5	## What this repo is
     6	
     7	SupplyGuard: a factory calls its approved suppliers (via the CALL-E phone API) to ask about a part shortage — availability, price, stock status, certification — and turns each call into a structured, typed "claim." It never compares those claims against the factory's own records or makes any purchasing decision; that's an explicitly out-of-scope later phase.
     8	
     9	The full behavioral spec (no code, just what goes in/out and why) lives at `docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md`. Read it before implementing anything in this domain — it defines the five building blocks (phone number safety, shared vocabulary, system of record, call script/answer sheet, call-to-claim conversion) and the non-negotiable rules below.
    10	
    11	The code lives in `backend/` (FastAPI app, outreach providers, persistence) and `packages/contracts/` (the shared models every slice builds against). Calls go through the official `calle` SDK — `client.calls.create()` to dial, `client.calls.wait_for_result()` to collect — both outbound, so no tunnel or public URL is involved.
    12	
    13	## Commands
    14	
    15	```bash
    16	# Run the whole suite. Nothing here touches the network.
    17	pytest test/ -v
    18	
    19	# Force rehearsal if .env has FAKE_CALLS=0, so the fake-provider tests pass
    20	FAKE_CALLS=1 pytest test/ -v
    21	
    22	# Start the API
    23	python -m uvicorn backend.main:app --port 8000
    24	```
    25	
    26	Two by-hand scripts, neither run by pytest: `test/try_fake_outreach.py` exercises the rehearsal flow, and `test/try_real_outreach.py` places one real, billed call and prints the resulting quote and transcript.
    27	
    28	Config is read from `.env` (gitignored; copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in `CALLE_API_KEY`, etc.). `FAKE_CALLS=0` is what enables real dialing — nothing else does.
    29	
    30	Finished quotes are written to `data/quotes/<case_id>/<task_id>.json` (gitignored: real phone numbers and transcripts). `STORE` is in-memory and dies with the process, so that directory is the only durable record of a call.
    31	
    32	## Non-negotiable domain rules
    33	
    34	These apply to all code in this repo:
    35	
    36	- **Phone numbers**: validate to E.164 the moment a number enters the system; mask (`+1******0199` style) everywhere it's displayed, logged, or printed. The *only* place a raw, unmasked number may appear is inside the literal outbound request body used to place the call.
    37	- **Rehearsal vs. live mode**: rehearsal (reading a saved/faked call result) is always the default. Live calling (actually dialing) is always an explicit, deliberate opt-in — never a fallback and never triggered by a merely-unset setting. No test, demo, or rehearsal run may touch the network.
    38	- **AI disclosure**: every call script must open with the AI disclosure (who it is, who it's calling for, that it won't commit to price/quantity/delivery, that it will end the call if asked for a human or to stop). This cannot be optional or skippable.
    39	- **"Unknown" is a first-class answer**: fields like price-quoted, certification-current, part-number-confirmed, and stock-status must allow "unknown" rather than forcing a guess. Turning a call result into a claim must never crash — a garbled/incomplete result becomes a claim with fields defaulted to "unknown"/zero and confidence 0, not an exception.
    40	- **Money** uses exact decimal precision, never float arithmetic that can drift.

Confirmed: read the requested audit-playbook sections (“Tech Debt & Architecture,” “DX & Tooling,” “Docs,” and “Finding format”), ran `entire status`, and inspected relevant checkpoint history. No files were modified.

### [ARCH-01] Establish the two-product layout and naming

- **Evidence**: `apps/web/app/layout.tsx:9-15` already names the product **SupplyOS**. `apps/web/app/prototype/README.md:33-40` states the intended boundary: ERP owns the Incident; SupplyOS owns sourcing. In contrast, `ui/package.json:2`, `ui/app/layout.tsx:14-17`, and `ui/app/cockpit/page.tsx:137-139` still identify the ERP surface as `ehl_hack`/`Stockout`.
- **Impact**: Users cannot tell the mock ERP from the actual product, and every launcher/doc must special-case the unexplained root `ui/`.
- **Effort**: M
- **Risk**: MED — paths affect launch scripts, imports, lockfiles, and docs.
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Move `ui/` to `apps/erp/`, rename its package to `@supplyos/erp`, and brand its metadata/navigation simply **ERP**. Keep `apps/web/` as **SupplyOS**. Update all path consumers together.

### [DEBT-02] Delete the orphaned `apps/api` artifact

- **Evidence**: The only tracked content beneath `apps/api/` is the binary `apps/api/backend/record/supplyguard.db`. The actual generated database is `backend/record/supplyguard.db` according to `run.py:232-239`; `.gitignore:56-57` ignores only that canonical location.
- **Impact**: `apps/api` looks like a second backend but contains no API source, causing precisely the backend/API ambiguity the user reported; it also commits a 156 KB generated database.
- **Effort**: S
- **Risk**: LOW — no code references `apps/api`.
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Delete `apps/api/`; broaden the DB ignore rule to cover accidental nested copies. Recorded intent from checkpoint `01M0PFZ1TESW8H311SWJ8FC96R` confirms this DB was produced while seeding a copied monorepo layout, not authored source.

### [DOCS-03] Replace the stale agent operating manual

- **Evidence**: `docs/PLAN.md:363` requires `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` to stay synchronized. `AGENTS.md:1-20` is only generic pointers, while `CLAUDE.md:7` says comparison and purchasing decisions are out of scope, contradicting the implemented target in `docs/PLAN.md:180-184`. `CLAUDE.md:17-23` runs only `test/` and the obsolete `backend.main` app; `CLAUDE.md:26` names nonexistent `test/try_real_outreach.py`; `CLAUDE.md:30` describes obsolete persistence.
- **Impact**: Agents receive incorrect architecture, commands, scope, and safety behavior before making changes.
- **Effort**: S
- **Risk**: LOW
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Make root `AGENTS.md` the concise source of truth for SupplyOS vs ERP, final directory boundaries, `run.py` commands, test gates, API entry point, and live-call safeguards; make `CLAUDE.md` reference or faithfully mirror it. Keep Next-specific generated instructions inside each Next app.
- **Note**: Missing `CONTEXT.md`/`docs/adr` is **not** evidence that AGENTS is stale: `docs/agents/domain.md:7-11` explicitly says those artifacts are optional and their absence should not be flagged.

### [DOCS-04] Rewrite the false tech-stack inventory

- **Evidence**: `docs/agents/tech-stack.md:4-10` claims Vinext, Vite, Cloudflare Workers/D1, and Drizzle; `docs/agents/tech-stack.md:14` claims Node’s test runner. Actual manifests show Next and Vitest in `ui/package.json:7-13,20` and Next in `apps/web/package.json:7-12,27`; Python/FastAPI dependencies are in `pyproject.toml:5-17`.
- **Impact**: Agents may introduce the wrong framework conventions, deployment assumptions, datastore, and test commands.
- **Effort**: S
- **Risk**: LOW
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Replace it with the actual stack: Next.js 16/React 19/Tailwind 4 for `apps/web` and `apps/erp`, FastAPI/Pydantic/SQLite/YAML for the backend, Vitest for ERP, pytest for Python, and the chosen Node package manager.

### [DOCS-05] Collapse obsolete plans and one-time prompts

- **Evidence**: `README.md:10-12` presents three competing sources of truth. `sourcing_agent_plan_v3.md:1,329-332` is an older distribution plan with naming still unresolved. `slice-b-core-api-erp-ui.md:3` says it is already built and contains broken root-relative links. `docs/prompts/slice-1-devin.md:7-10` instructs agents not to add FastAPI or SQLite despite both now existing. `docs/mvp-flow.md:5-11` and `docs/mvp-slices.md:71-79` describe the old Vercel/deferred-CALL-E phase. `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-22-slice-c-calle-outreach.md:11,41` points at nonexistent or superseded paths.
- **Impact**: A future agent can follow a valid-looking but obsolete build phase and reintroduce discarded architecture.
- **Effort**: M
- **Risk**: LOW — Git preserves the historical material.
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Keep `docs/PLAN.md` as product intent but mark/update its resolved decisions and SupplyOS name. Delete completed one-time implementation plans/prompts (`sourcing_agent_plan_v3.md`, `slice-b-core-api-erp-ui.md`, the Slice 1 prompt, completed superpowers plan); replace `mvp-flow`/`mvp-slices` with one current flow/architecture document.

### [DEBT-06] Remove the unrelated Cursor design artifact

- **Evidence**: `DESIGN.md:3-4` identifies itself as `Cursor-design-analysis` for an AI code editor and Cursor marketing site. Remaining code references are comments in `ui/app/layout.tsx:7-10`, `ui/components/cockpit/primitives.tsx:5`, `ui/components/theme-provider.tsx:6-12`, and `ui/lib/stages.ts:3-9`.
- **Impact**: A 537-line unrelated brand specification appears authoritative and keeps “Cursor Orange/CursorGothic” terminology embedded in the ERP.
- **Effort**: S
- **Risk**: LOW — it is not imported at runtime.
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Delete `DESIGN.md`; rewrite the four comments to describe local ERP tokens directly. Preserve or deliberately redesign the actual CSS separately.

### [DEBT-07] Delete shipped throwaway prototypes and unused image assets

- **Evidence**: `apps/web/app/prototype/README.md:1-3` explicitly says the folder is throwaway and not the product; `:17-23` says variant E was selected. `apps/web/app/prototype/cockpit-screens.html:6-8,368-370` repeats that it is throwaway. Production already uses the selected background at `apps/web/app/page.tsx:7-10`. A repository-wide reference scan found `background-3.png` entirely unused; backgrounds 1 and 2 are used only by prototype variants at `apps/web/components/prototype/website-prototype-variants.tsx:7-12,70-76`.
- **Impact**: Prototype routes/components and roughly 5 MB of obsolete assets ship with production and obscure the selected UI.
- **Effort**: S
- **Risk**: LOW
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Delete `apps/web/app/prototype/`, `apps/web/components/prototype/`, and backgrounds 1–3; retain background 4 and production components.

### [DX-08] Make `run.py` the single launcher and remove wrapper sprawl

- **Evidence**: `run.py:13-16` declares itself the cross-platform replacement; `package.json:5-14` adds a Node wrapper solely to invoke it; `.npmrc:1-4` admits the root package owns no dependencies; `pnpm-workspace.yaml:1-3` defines no workspace packages. `Makefile:22,38-39,47,57` hardcodes `ui/`, while its `clean` target at `Makefile:59-60` recursively deletes case directories.
- **Impact**: The same command surface is maintained through Python, Make, pnpm, shell, CMD, and Node; moves require editing all of them, and `make clean` can erase case artifacts.
- **Effort**: S–M
- **Risk**: MED — teammates may have muscle memory around `make` or `pnpm`.
- **Confidence**: HIGH
- **Fix sketch**: Keep `run.py` plus thin `run.sh`/`run.cmd`; update it for `apps/erp` and `apps/web`. Remove `Makefile`, root `package.json`, `.npmrc`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and `scripts/run-py.mjs` unless the team deliberately converts to a real workspace.

### [DX-09] Remove the duplicate Python dependency manifest

+# SupplyOS
 
-### Issue tracker

+We will not trade these away as we iterate.

+2. **Claims are not facts.** What a supplier says stays separate from the factory's trusted records.
+3. **Self-checking decisions.** Compliance and landed-cost logic are executable and tested before a recommendation ships.
+4. **Human approval.** The agent recommends. A human approves by merging the pull request.
+
+## Who is who
+
+- **you** — the agent reading this file and changing this repo.
+- **we, us** — the maintainers and developers you are talking to.
+- **user** — the person resolving a factory shortage.
+- **supplier** — the party contacted for availability, price, stock status, and certification.
+
+Use the domain words from `docs/PLAN.md` and `docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md`: Incident, Supplier Record, Claim, Candidate, Outreach Task, Landed Cost, Strategy, and Decision. Do not invent synonyms.
+
+## How it works
+
+Shortage trigger → Devin Session → system-of-record lookup → supplier outreach through CALL-E → structured Claims → compliance and landed-cost checks → Decision → human approval by merging the PR. The cockpit renders progress and the final state.
+
+## Where code lives
+
+- `backend/` — the FastAPI service: `backend.api.main:app` on :8010. Devin tool endpoints and the cockpit read API in one process.
+- `backend/record/` — the system of record behind one port, two adapters: `mock_erp.py` (YAML, the seed source) and `sqlite_erp.py` (the compiled `.db`, a build artifact).
+- `packages/contracts/` — the frozen contract: Pydantic models, plus the JSON Schema and TypeScript types generated from them. Shared by every consumer; changes need a group ping.
+- `orchestrator/` — the CLI that drives a case through the stages. Thin: the logic belongs in `backend/`.
+- `apps/erp/` — the ERP Next.js app: item master, stock, cases, cockpit. Runs fixture-only with no backend.
+- `apps/web/` — the SupplyOS cockpit and chat, proxying to the API through `app/backend/[...path]`.
+- `cases/` — case artifacts, one directory per case.
+- `docs/PLAN.md` — MVP architecture, contracts, slices, delivery plan.
+- `docs/agents/` — task-specific agent guidance.
+
+Each of those directories has its own `AGENTS.md`. Read it before changing code there.
+
+## Three ways to hurt this repo
+
+1. **An accidental real call.** Rehearsal is always the default. Live calling requires every explicit guard and can spend money or contact a person.
+2. **A Claim treated as truth.** Supplier statements and trusted factory records remain separate types through every layer.
+3. **A shortcut around the audit trail.** Decisions retain executable checks and human review, not opaque prose or automatic purchasing.
+
+## Non-negotiable domain rules
+
+- Validate phone numbers as E.164 when they enter the system. Mask them everywhere except the literal outbound request body.
+- Keep rehearsal offline and deterministic. Live mode is an explicit opt-in (`LIVE_CALLS=yes-place-real-calls` **and** `FAKE_CALLS=0`), never a fallback.
+- Start every call with the mandatory AI disclosure. End the call when the callee requests a human or asks to stop.
+- Model missing or unclear answers as `unknown`. Convert unusable call results into confidence-zero Claims instead of crashing.
+- Use exact decimal arithmetic for money, serialized as a string. No floats.
+- Use only reserved fictional phone numbers in code, tests, fixtures, and documentation. Keep secrets in the local environment.
+- Produce purchase recommendations only. A human approves any purchase through review.
+
+## Taste
+
+Prefer pure functions and narrow adapters. Keep external systems at the boundary. Build fixtures before live integrations. Keep policy rules and cost functions deterministic. One shared contract serves backend types, JSON Schema, and UI consumers.
+
+Comments explain how a thing is used or why a constraint exists. Prefer one useful comment over line-by-line narration.
+
+If a rule here conflicts with the requested task, explain the conflict and get developer approval before breaking it.
+
+## Verifying
+
+Use the smallest proof that covers the change. `run.py` works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux.

+```bash
+python run.py setup   # once per machine: venv, npm install, build the database
+python run.py test    # backend tests + ERP typecheck. Never touches the network.
+python run.py         # API on :8010 and the ERP on :3000
+```
+
+- Backend or contracts change: `python run.py test`.
+- Frontend change: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` in the app you touched; `npm test` in `apps/erp` for the route handlers.
+- Live CALL-E: only when the developer explicitly asks for a real call and all guards are set.
+
+Never run a live test as general verification. A user-visible behavior change must update the matching spec, plan, or design document in the same change.
+
+## Pull requests
+
+Never create a pull request unless the developer asks. Do not create a draft by default. When asked, create a ready-for-review pull request and include the relevant Devin Session URL.
+
+Never force-push or amend unless the developer asks. Do not push directly to `main`.
+
+## Docs
+
+- `docs/PLAN.md` — before changing product scope, architecture, contracts, case artifacts, orchestration, or the demo flow.
+- `DESIGN.md` — the design tokens the ERP app implements: colours, type scale, spacing.
+- `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` and `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` — when creating, reading, or labeling GitHub issues.
+- `docs/agents/domain.md` — when changing domain vocabulary or architectural decisions.
+- `docs/agents/tech-stack.md` — the tools this repo uses and their documentation links.
+
+Durable truth lives in the files above. GitHub issues hold work in flight.

-# CLAUDE.md
-
-This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
-
-## What this repo is
-
-SupplyGuard: a factory calls its approved suppliers (via the CALL-E phone API) to ask about a part shortage — availability, price, stock status, certification — and turns each call into a structured, typed "claim." It never compares those claims against the factory's own records or makes any purchasing decision; that's an explicitly out-of-scope later phase.
-
-The full behavioral spec (no code, just what goes in/out and why) lives at `docs/specs/supplyguard-plan-1-foundation-spec.md`. Read it before implementing anything in this domain — it defines the five building blocks (phone number safety, shared vocabulary, system of record, call script/answer sheet, call-to-claim conversion) and the non-negotiable rules below.
-
-The code lives in `backend/` (FastAPI app, outreach providers, persistence) and `packages/contracts/` (the shared models every slice builds against). Calls go through the official `calle` SDK — `client.calls.create()` to dial, `client.calls.wait_for_result()` to collect — both outbound, so no tunnel or public URL is involved.
-
-## Commands
-
-```bash
-# Run the whole suite. Nothing here touches the network.
-pytest test/ -v
-
-# Force rehearsal if .env has FAKE_CALLS=0, so the fake-provider tests pass
-FAKE_CALLS=1 pytest test/ -v
-
-# Start the API
-python -m uvicorn backend.main:app --port 8000
-```
-
-Two by-hand scripts, neither run by pytest: `test/try_fake_outreach.py` exercises the rehearsal flow, and `test/try_real_outreach.py` places one real, billed call and prints the resulting quote and transcript.
-
-Config is read from `.env` (gitignored; copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in `CALLE_API_KEY`, etc.). `FAKE_CALLS=0` is what enables real dialing — nothing else does.
-
-Finished quotes are written to `data/quotes/<case_id>/<task_id>.json` (gitignored: real phone numbers and transcripts). `STORE` is in-memory and dies with the process, so that directory is the only durable record of a call.
-
-## Non-negotiable domain rules
-
-These apply to all code in this repo:
-

## Acceptance criteria
- Entire remains enabled with git hooks installed.
- Stale or duplicate sessions no longer affect attribution.
- A new real agent commit is checkpoint-linked and visible after sync.
- Any backfilled checkpoint is evidence-backed by its transcript.

## Notes
Current setup is healthy: hooks and agent integrations are installed, and checkpoint storage is already using the git-refs store. Historic gaps partly predate restored hooks and also include manual/setup/merge commits, which should remain unlinked." --label "ready-for-agent
